correctness.rationale: The proof decomposes the tail exactly into singleton, pair, and triple Möbius faces. Singleton tails are exact. The zero pair is exactly independent and supplies the known two-Pareto logarithm. Each negative pair is O(t^{-2}) by an explicit Gaussian-conditioning and dominated-convergence argument. The triple face is O(t^{-2}) by a bounded all-lower Gaussian copula density (Stieltjes inverse) plus fixed-width shell control when one reciprocal score is bounded. Quantile and size formulas follow by direct asymptotic inversion. No finite computation substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the minimal genuinely mixed zero/negative one-sided Gaussian slice of an explicitly stated 2026 open problem. It identifies a structural boundary: an exactly zero Gaussian edge alone preserves the critical logarithm, while strict negative edges and the three-way interaction drop to O(t^{-2}). The resulting critical-value and type-I-error coefficients quantify precisely how much full-independence calibration overcorrects at small levels.
